# The step of a dot product of one limb, on arrays of the program: one fused multiply-add of the guarded elements

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `dot_entry_step_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

$s + x y$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y).$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dot(x, y)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 1>>` | the step of the loop the function calls, once per element; not `constexpr`; rounds; in the lane order of the build, or, with `kairn::sequential`, in the sequential order (loop `dot_1_entry`; each factor guarded, rule R3 on the factors of a fused operation) |
| `dot(sequential, x, y)` | `Sequential`, `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>` | `Reduction<Expansion<T, 1>>` |  |
| `conv(x, y, z)` | `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<const T, 1>`, `SoAView<T, 1>` | `bool` | each coefficient a sequential `dot_1_entry` (loop `conv_1_entry`; each factor guarded) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the functions are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/batch.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` does not include; a view of `T` is taken where the table writes a view of `const T`. They take no marker: a function on arrays compiles only while the kernels of its loop are proved ([Functions on arrays](batch.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t = \mathrm{RN}(s + x y)$: the number of the format nearest to $s + x y$, ties to even.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `dot_entry_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/StepKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/StepKernels.v), against `dot_entry_step_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions dot_entry_step_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition dot_entry_step_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s x y : R,
  fmt emin prec s ->
  fmt emin prec x ->
  fmt emin prec y ->
  let t := dot_entry_step_1 emin prec tie_even s x y in
  fmt emin prec t /\
  t = RN emin prec (s + (x * y)).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `dot_entry_step_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** dot_step_1 on the guarded elements (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation). **License:** proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/dot_entry_step_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/dot_entry_step_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The step of dot_1_entry, the dot product of one limb of arrays the program supplies: dot_step_1,
# s <- RN(x y + s), on the elements guarded (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation:
# architecture.md). dot_step_1 only multiplies its elements, which R3 alone does not guard; but a
# compiler that sees one factor to be 1 (an array of ones the program fills) rewrites fma(x, 1, s)
# as x + s and fuses the program's product x = a b into that addition (Clang 18 on x86-64 and Apple
# clang 21 under -ffp-contract=fast). After the guards each factor is a number of the format, the
# rounded product a b at most. Its claims are those of dot_step_1: the guard is the identity on
# numbers of the format.

gx = guard(x)
gy = guard(y)
t  = fma(gx, gy, s)
```
